holidays.name: National Freezer Pop Day
holidays.description: Grab a plastic sleeve of brightly colored, sugary ice and snip off the top. Today is for celebrating the humble freezer pop, which cools you down and stains your tongue a color not found in nature. Bonus points if you squeeze it from the bottom and wage a brain-freeze battle with your siblings.
holidays.origin: The Jel Sert Company, makers of Otter Pops, founded this observance in 2020. They wanted people to remember childhood summer days spent eating freezer pops.
holidays.funFact: The holiday was created by the company behind Otter Pops, a freezer pop brand. Its treats come in long plastic sleeves that kids have been snipping open for generations.

holidays.name: National Ice Cream Sundae Day
holidays.description: Today is the day to pile scoops of ice cream into a bowl and cover them with hot fudge, whipped cream, sprinkles, and a cherry. A build-your-own sundae party is the traditional way to celebrate. Guests bring their favorite toppings, and nobody judges the ones that make no sense.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance that falls during National Ice Cream Month in July. Its exact origin is unclear.
holidays.funFact: July 8 is a good day for frozen treats. It also hosts National Freezer Pop Day, so you can have a full dessert crawl.

holidays.name: Math 2.0 Day
holidays.description: Math fans, this one is for you. Today is a playful nod to the idea that math can be updated, upgraded, and made more fun. Dust off some math drills, solve a puzzle, or challenge a friend to a number game.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is listed among July 8's quirky celebrations.
holidays.funFact: The name borrows the 'version 2.0' language of software updates. It suggests that even old subjects like arithmetic can get a fresh release.
